newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-WORLD CUP CHAMPION ALPHAND RETIRES.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WORLD CUP CHAMPION ALPHAND RETIRES.

text.p: Alpine skier Luc Alphand, the overall World Cup champion, said on Thursday he was retiring from the sport.
The 31-year-old Frenchman said he had considered going on until the Winter Olympics in February next year in Nagano, Japan.
"It was not an easy decision to take," he told a news conference. "Eighty percent of the people around me wanted me to carry on but I have a family to look after."
Alphand, whose 13-year career has been hampered by a string of injuries, had established himself as the world's best speed racer over the last few seasons.
In March he became the first Frenchman to win the overall World Cup since Jean-Claude Killy in 1968.
